ENSX1004.description: Fundamentals of Materials Engineering introduces students to the basic principles, structures and properties of engineering materials. The unit also covers: failure modes of materials; (plastic yielding, fatigue, fracture and creep); thermo-mechanical behaviour of materials; recycling of materials and sustainability in the context of recycle and reuse; and the impact of materials failure on society and the environment.
ENSX1004.outcomes: Students are able to (1) describe basic classes of engineering materials, their properties, structures and applications.; (2) explain the relationship between stress and strain in metals, ceramics and polymers; (3) determine both the elastic and plastic properties of a material from tensile stress-strain curves.; (4) recognise various failure modes of engineering materials and explain design principles that could be employed to prevent in-service failure.; (5) identify common forms of industrial corrosion and degradation of materials ; and (6) discuss recycling of materials and the impact of materials selection on society and the environment.
ENSX1004.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) quizzes; (2) laboratories; and (3) examinations. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
